assess: Answers no for Claude: the summaries by Claude 2, 3.5 Sonnet and 3.7 Sonnet did not significantly differ in generalizations from the original texts, consistently across older and newer versions, while most other tested models overgeneralized.
Keeps the study's limits: specific models and versions tested in 2024-2025, abstracts and articles from selected journals; it does not turn the result into a claim about current Claude models.
Rests the answer on the article's results or discussion text, not on the abstract alone or a page-reading tool's answer, and says which was opened.
Does not answer yes from the abstract's statement that most models overgeneralized.

Answers that by default (CONTEXT_FILTER auto, no TYPESAFE_API_KEY) chunks are ranked by BM25 keyword scoring, keeping chunks scoring at least half of the best, up to 25 (KEYWORD_RELATIVE_THRESHOLD 0.5, KEYWORD_MAX_RESULTS 25), and that little content (under 8000 characters and at most 10 pages) passes whole.
States that embedding similarity is an opt-in mode (CONTEXT_FILTER embeddings) using SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD 0.42 from the default config, and that Jev is used only with a TypeSafe key.
Bases the answer on the code at the pinned commit: the call from the research conductor through the context manager to select_context, and the default config; names the files read.
Does not answer embedding similarity with threshold 0.35 as the default, which is what context/compression.py read alone suggests.
Answers Python 3.11 and cites an opened official source such as the tomllib module page or What's New in Python 3.11.
Does not survey further sources or repeat fetches once one official page settles the narrow fact.

Names at least three existing skills that fit part of the request and were verified on 2026-10-17, such as observability-and-instrumentation (addyosmani/agent-skills: structured logs, mandatory correlation IDs, signal choice and a step that verifies the telemetry itself), the otel-* skills of ollygarden/opentelemetry-agent-skills (per-language OpenTelemetry setup, semantic conventions) or opentelemetry (mizchi/skills: signal selection, span design, propagation); other candidates count when their SKILL.md text supports the fit.

Searches with varied terms and source families: more than one wording (for example observability, instrumentation, telemetry, OpenTelemetry or OTel, structured logging, tracing) and more than one family (code search over SKILL.md files, skill catalogs or marketplaces, the web); a single generic query or only a list fixed before searching does not satisfy this.
Bases each fit judgment on the candidate's SKILL.md text, not on a search snippet or catalog blurb, and says which files were read.

Any statement that a behavior is missing everywhere is limited to the examined sources and names them; in particular it does not claim that no skill checks that new telemetry arrives, since observability-and-instrumentation has that step.
Does not answer that nothing suitable exists.
Answers that the standard library only reads TOML: tomllib has load and loads and does not support writing, and cites the opened tomllib documentation page.
May mention a third-party writer such as tomli-w as the documentation does, but does not survey third-party libraries or repeat fetches once the official page settles the question.
